name: Closed benchmarks for network community structure characterization
description: Characterizing the community structure of complex networks is a key challenge in many scientific fields. Very diverse algorithms and methods have been proposed to this end, many working reasonably well in specific situations. However, no consensus has emerged on which of these methods is the best to use in practice. In part, this is due to the fact that testing their performance requires the generation of a comprehensive, standard set of synthetic benchmarks, a goal not yet fully achieved. Here, we present a type of benchmark that we call "closed", in which an initial network of known community structure is progressively converted into a second network whose communities are also known. This approach differs from all previously published ones, in which networks evolve toward randomness. The use of this type of benchmark allows us to monitor the transformation of the community structure of a network. evaluation_method: variation of information, normalized mutual information, modularity
reputation: A classic and widely cited benchmark framework in network science for evaluating community detection methods, especially on synthetic graphs with known ground truth.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; primarily used for algorithmic community detection evaluation rather than a single standardized leaderboard score. Results depend heavily on graph generation settings and the chosen clustering metric.
